solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Game bird caught in blurry photos (5-2-2)

indicators.note: the bird is held inside the other letters
photos that are blurry have their letters out of focus, so rearrange them

blocks.note: rearranged to SHOOTP
the flightless Australian bird

annotation.surface: A birdwatcher's snapshots of a game bird have all come out blurred.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Game bird' reads as one thing, grouse or pheasant, but 'Game' is the definition and the bird sits inside the jumbled photos.
annotation.definitionFit: A shoot-'em-up is a video game built around shooting enemies.

entries.clue: Japanese scoff, upsetting setters on docked vessel (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down, reading it bottom to top
a docked tail is cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the setters speak of themselves as US; turned up it is SU
docked of its last letter, SHI

annotation.surface: Sailors grumble about Japanese food served aboard a ship in port.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' is British slang for food as a noun, not mockery, and 'docked' means cut short, not moored.
annotation.definitionFit: Sushi is Japanese food, and scoff is informal British for food.

entries.clue: Veteran audibly shuffled cards (3,4)

indicators.note: take the sound of the word, not its spelling

blocks.note: a veteran is old
in card games to make the cards is to shuffle them, so shuffled cards are made

annotation.surface: An old hand at the table mixes the deck noisily.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shuffled' is MADE through card-table jargon, where making the pack means shuffling it; said aloud it gives MAID.
annotation.definitionFit: Old Maid is a card game, so the answer names the cards played.

entries.clue: Drink alone in a flirtatious way (9)

blocks.note: a cup of tea
one at a time, on one's own

annotation.surface: Someone having a drink on their own while flirting.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a lone drinker making eyes at the room; 'alone' supplies an adverb, matching the adverbial definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To tease someone can be to flirt with them playfully, so teasingly means flirtatiously.

entries.clue: Passing reminder of internet phenomenon on broken monitor (7,4)

indicators.note: the letters of the word are broken apart and rearranged

blocks.note: an idea or image that spreads online
rearranged to NTOMORI

annotation.surface: A viral image pops up as a reminder on a cracked computer screen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like 'fleeting', but here it means dying: the answer is a reminder of death.
annotation.definitionFit: A memento mori, Latin for 'remember you must die', is an object that reminds us of our own passing.

entries.clue: Fixed up mate with stock option (3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: farmyard sense: a ram tups a ewe, mating with her; the letters then turn up the column

annotation.surface: Someone arranged for a friend to be offered a share option.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mate' is the farmyard verb, TUP, what a ram does; 'up' turns it over in a down clue, and the result also means fixed or placed.
annotation.definitionFit: Put means placed or fixed in position, and a put is an option to sell stock at a set price.

entries.clue: Garlic mayonnaise: superior colloid used regularly (5)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, every other one

blocks.note: A1, first-rate, written with I for 1
the second, fourth and sixth letters of cOlLoId

annotation.surface: A food scientist praises mayonnaise as a first-class emulsion.
annotation.walkthrough: Mayonnaise really is a colloid, which makes the chemistry look like the definition; 'superior' is A1.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: aioli is the Provençal name for exactly this sauce, mayonnaise pounded with garlic.

entries.clue: Some propose arresting revolutionary fabulist (5)

indicators.note: only part of the words is used
the words hold the answer inside them
turned right round, read backwards

blocks.note: the letters straddle the gap: the last four of propOSE plus the A of Arresting, read backwards

annotation.surface: A radical storyteller is to be taken into custody, someone suggests.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs backwards across 'propose arresting', starting in 'propose' and taking the A of 'arresting'.
annotation.definitionFit: Aesop is the Greek teller of fables, the fabulist of the tortoise and the hare.

entries.clue: Art school led by Boris, boundlessly imaginative at first (7)

indicators.note: the other part comes first
without its bounds, the first and last letters
what comes at first in a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: bORIs without its outer letters
a gam is a school of whales
its first letter

annotation.surface: An art college run by a creative Boris.
annotation.walkthrough: 'School' is not a college but GAM, a group of whales.
annotation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of paper folding.

entries.clue: I see rising dons prone to imprecision in prestigious universities (3,6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top
to don is to put on, so one part is put around the other

blocks.note: as written
the see, or bishop's diocese, of Ely; rising it is YLE
vague, wrapped round YLE as V-YLE-AGUE

annotation.surface: Academics at elite universities stand up to speak loosely.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I see' is not a phrase of understanding: 'see' is a diocese, here Ely, an English cathedral city.
annotation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is the group of eight old, prestigious universities in the north-east US.

entries.clue: Piece of pretentiousness by administrative subdivision (7)

blocks.note: putting on side is giving oneself airs
a branch of an organisation

annotation.surface: A bureaucratic department produces a bit of pomposity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece' is slang for a gun, not a fragment; 'side' is British for airs and graces.
annotation.definitionFit: A piece is slang for a handgun, a sidearm worn at the hip.

entries.clue: Supposing irritable hosts swear (7)

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: short-tempered
on the supposition that

annotation.surface: What if a grumpy host starts cursing?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swear' reads as cursing, but it means to declare on oath.
annotation.definitionFit: Swear in its legal sense, to state something on oath, which is what a witness does in the box.

entries.clue: National spirit of Turkey articulated by Istanbul’s leader (5)

indicators.note: spoken, so take the sound
the leader of a word is the letter that goes in front of the rest

blocks.note: first letter of Istanbul
raki is the Turkish aniseed spirit

annotation.surface: An Istanbul official speaks of Turkey's national character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'National spirit' looks like patriotism, but 'National' alone is the definition, a citizen, and the spirit is the drink raki.
annotation.definitionFit: National as a noun, a citizen of some country; the answer is a citizen of Iraq, so a definition by example.

entries.clue: Sign on door of Lloyd’s underwriter with denture (9)

blocks.note: a Name is an individual backer of insurance at Lloyd's of London
a dental plate holds false teeth

annotation.surface: The notice on the office door of an insurer with false teeth.
annotation.walkthrough: Lloyd's of London is the insurance market; its private underwriters are called Names.
annotation.definitionFit: A nameplate is the sign on a door giving the occupant's name.

entries.clue: Curse mass beer delivery (11)

blocks.note: the physics symbol for mass
a kind of beer
a speaker's delivery, the way words are spoken

annotation.surface: Someone swears at a big shipment of beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests a dray at the pub door, but here it is a speaker's manner of speaking.
annotation.definitionFit: A malediction is a curse, a spoken wish for harm.

entries.clue: Whit appointment curtailed and put back (3)

indicators.note: its tail, the last letter, is cut off
a word put back is set in reverse, its last letter now first

blocks.note: a date is an appointment; curtailed, DAT

annotation.surface: A Whitsun meeting is cut short and postponed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Whit' looks like the holiday Whitsun, but it is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit'.
annotation.definitionFit: A whit and a tad are both a very small amount.

entries.clue: Restrained method of painting walls of temple (9)

indicators.note: the outside letters, the walls around the word

blocks.note: painting with pigment bound in egg yolk
the outer letters of TemplE

annotation.surface: A discreet technique for painting a temple's walls.
annotation.walkthrough: The walls of a temple are literally painted in tempera in many churches, which makes 'walls' look physical rather than a letter instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Temperate means moderate or self-restrained.

entries.clue: Handsome Wenceslas perhaps embracing ladies? (4-7)

indicators.note: one part wraps its arms around the other

blocks.note: Good King Wenceslas of the carol
the ladies is a women's lavatory, a loo

annotation.surface: Was the handsome Wenceslas fond of hugging women?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good King Wenceslas' is a Christmas carol; 'ladies' is the ladies' toilet, the LOO, not women at all.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both adjectives describe an attractive appearance.

entries.clue: Public fury over introduction of stealth taxes (9)

indicators.note: a word's introduction is where it begins, its first letter

blocks.note: open, not hidden
anger
its first letter

annotation.surface: Voters are furious at stealth taxes being brought in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taxes' is a verb, to strain someone, not a noun; in a down clue 'over' just puts IRE on top of S.
annotation.definitionFit: To tax someone is to wear them out, and to overtire is to exhaust.

entries.clue: Spooner’s figurine of canine pet (11)

indicators.note: swap the opening sounds of two words, as Dr Spooner did

blocks.note: a model of a collie, with the first sounds swapped

annotation.surface: Spooner owns a china ornament of his pet dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like the dog, but it is the verb, to pamper.
annotation.definitionFit: To mollycoddle is to pet or pamper someone excessively.

entries.clue: US writer from South interrupting fat cat (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, read from the bottom up
breaks into the middle of the other word

blocks.note: pig fat
Edgar Allan Poe; read from the south it is EOP

annotation.surface: An American author from the South breaks in on a rich fat cat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fat cat' reads as a wealthy person, but 'fat' is LARD and 'cat' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: cat here covers the big cats of the wild, and the spotted leopard is one of them.

entries.clue: Good American English (3)

blocks.note: abbreviation for the United States
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A nod of approval for American English.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good' is the noun sense, benefit, as in 'what's the good of it?', so it swaps for use.
annotation.definitionFit: 'What good is it?' and 'what use is it?' mean the same: good as benefit is use.

entries.clue: Argue angrily about doctor’s offence (7)

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about in temper
goes around the other part

blocks.note: rearranged to URAGE
Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

annotation.surface: Having a furious row about a doctor's misconduct.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Argue angrily' looks like one idea, but ARGUE is the fodder and 'angrily' its instruction; 'offence' is taking offence, not a crime.
annotation.definitionFit: The word survives almost only in the idiom 'take umbrage', where it means resentment felt at a slight.

entries.clue: Number one fan? (9)

blocks.note: reads as the top spot, first place; in fact it is slang for oneself, as in looking after number one
reads as a supporter of some star; here a devotee of oneself, and the question mark flags the twist

annotation.surface: Someone's biggest supporter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number one fan' means the keenest supporter, but read as a fan of number one, oneself, it is an egomaniac.
annotation.definitionFit: An egomaniac is obsessed with themselves, looking after number one.

entries.clue: Despise officer losing heart after minor injury (5)

indicators.note: the inside is lost, leaving the outer letters
the officer's letters come after the injury's, so they are placed second

blocks.note: actual bodily harm, the lesser charge of assault in English law
OfficeR without its heart

annotation.surface: Someone scorns a policeman who goes soft after a slight injury.
annotation.walkthrough: ABH, actual bodily harm, is the English legal charge below GBH, grievous bodily harm.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the answer is a stronger, more formal verb for regarding something with loathing.

entries.clue: Forbidden love on flying boat (5)

indicators.note: the letters are sent flying and land in a new order

blocks.note: rearranged to TABO
zero in tennis scoring, shaped like O

annotation.surface: A secret romance conducted on a seaplane.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Forbidden love' reads as an illicit affair, but the definition is 'Forbidden' and love is only the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: A word borrowed from Tongan for what social or religious custom prohibits, so it swaps directly for forbidden.

entries.clue: Crustless toast on income support in refuge (5)

indicators.note: remove the outside, the crusts at each end

blocks.note: tOASt without its outer letters
abbreviation for the British welfare benefit

annotation.surface: Someone living on benefits eats toast with the crusts cut off in a shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: Income Support is a British means-tested benefit, abbreviated IS.
annotation.definitionFit: An oasis is a place of refuge, like water in a desert.

entries.clue: Essentially unhappy bachelor, lost and disconcerted (7)

indicators.note: at its essence, the middle letter

blocks.note: the middle letter of unhAppy
Bachelor of Arts
as in shed pounds, got rid of

annotation.surface: A miserable single man, adrift and confused.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bachelor' is not an unmarried man but the degree BA.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both describe someone embarrassed and thrown off balance.

entries.clue: Taunt policeman with face of granite (3)

indicators.note: the front, the first letter

blocks.note: Detective Inspector
its first letter

annotation.surface: A stony-faced detective mocks a suspect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Face of granite' suggests a stern expression, but it only gives the letter G.
annotation.definitionFit: Noun sense: a pointed remark made at someone's expense, as in 'a dig at the boss'.

entries.clue: Incursions and raids on Barking (7)

indicators.note: barking mad, so the letters go crazy

blocks.note: the seven letters of both words together, to be scrambled

annotation.surface: A report of raids on Barking, a district of East London.
annotation.walkthrough: Barking is a place in East London, but here it is 'barking mad', the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the military sense: raids pushing into enemy ground, as in 'make inroads'.

entries.clue: Cockney believed that female ancestor (5)

indicators.note: a Cockney drops the H at the start of words

blocks.note: HELD, as in held a view, without its H
HER without its H

annotation.surface: A Londoner trusted that woman as a forebear.
annotation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent drops H, so both 'held' and 'her' lose it.
annotation.definitionFit: A looser sense: one's elders are those born before, the older generations, which stretches to forebears.

entries.clue: Criminals dread following grand old monarch and son (9)

indicators.note: this part comes after the other

blocks.note: a grand, a thousand pounds, is G
anxious fear
Elizabeth Regina
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: Crooks fear an old king and his son.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grand old monarch' reads as one royal, but 'grand' is only G.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: members of organised crime gangs, the mobsters of film.
